ITEM (1) -> 017.002-T, WITH A MATERIAL PREMISE CORRECTION: this entry asserted addLongPathPrefix's \\.\ device-namespace branch is 'currently unreachable given filepath.IsAbs's own device-path handling'. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE. Measured this cycle with an isolated go run probe: filepath.IsAbs returns TRUE for \\.\C:\foo (VolumeName \\.\C:), \\.\PhysicalDrive0, \\.\UNC\srv\sh\x, and for a 307-character \\.\-prefixed path. The !filepath.IsAbs early return does NOT shadow the branch -- THE BRANCH IS REACHABLE. What is actually true is narrower: within the guard order (\\?\ -> \\.\ -> \\) the branch is REACHABLE BUT BEHAVIOURALLY REDUNDANT, because the immediately-following generic \\ guard returns the identical value for any \\.\ input. Independently confirmed by the Correctness Reviewer during adversarial plan review. 017.002-T therefore keeps the branch (deletion rejected: removes self-documenting intent and couples correctness to the adjacent guard's continued existence), locks its observable verdict with an order-independent characterization test, and corrects the stale prose. A panic/unreachability assertion was REJECTED BY NAME -- the premise is false, and docs/compound/build-errors/go-race-requires-cgo-fails-closed-2026-09-03.md records a prior incident of exactly this failure mode (defensive scaffolding on an unverified premise becoming review-finding surface for no safety benefit). ITEM (2) -> 017.003-T: MAX_PATH threshold made UTF-16-code-unit-aware. Measured: 200 x U+00E9 = 400 UTF-8 bytes / 200 UTF-16 units; 100 x U+1F600 = 400 bytes / 200 units. UTF-8 byte length is ALWAYS >= UTF-16 code-unit count (1->1, 2->1, 3->1, 4->2), so the existing proxy fires at or before the true limit -- it can only produce a FALSE POSITIVE, never a false negative. CONFIRMED: this is a PRECISION improvement, NOT a correctness or security defect, and framing it as a vulnerability fix is an explicit anti-goal. A rune count was rejected (a surrogate pair is 1 rune but 2 UTF-16 code units, which would introduce the false negative the current code never has). The deliberation's original 'non-allocating bespoke counter' option was WITHDRAWN at plan review as gold-plating; 017.003-T uses utf16.Encode or a plain range accumulator. Plan review additionally surfaced and ACCEPTED decision D-10: dropping the \\?\ prefix in the precision-gain band re-enables ordinary Win32 normalization (trailing dot/space stripping, reserved device names CON/NUL/AUX) for those paths, which is exactly how every sub-MAX_PATH path already behaves today.
